pr_title: Add support for listening to tcp handles to in the Sockets transport
pr_body:
- Make ListenHandleTests shared across both transports
- Added API to signify ownership semantics of the file handle

Fixes #20842
pr_comments:
@Tratcher @halter73 this is good to go.

cc @dotnet/aspnet-api-review can I get a review

Thank you for submitting this for API review. This will be reviewed by @dotnet/aspnet-api-review at the next meeting of the ASP.NET Core API Review group. Please ensure you take a look at [the API review process documentation](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/master/docs/APIReviewProcess.md) and ensure that:

* The PR contains changes to the reference-assembly that describe the API change. **Or**, you have included a snippet of reference-assembly-style code that illustrates the API change.
* The PR describes the impact to users, both positive (useful new APIs) and negative (breaking changes).
* Someone is assigned to "champion" this change in the meeting, and they understand the impact and design of the change.

Can you move ListenHandleTests to Kestrel's main shared FunctionalTests directory so it's run as part of Sockets.FunctionalTests in addition to Libuv.FunctionalTests?

We should also add a version of [CanListenToOpenTcpSocketHandle](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/40e0649785feafc6c59337492eb1c5c5c081d663/src/Servers/Kestrel/test/Libuv.FunctionalTests/ListenHandleTests.cs#L25) which sets OwnsHandle to false and verifies the server can successfully be started and stopped with the same handle twice. Otherwise, we have no test coverage for the new OwnsHandle API.

> Can you move ListenHandleTests to Kestrel's main shared FunctionalTests directory so it's run as part of Sockets.FunctionalTests in addition to Libuv.FunctionalTests?

It's already moved and running for both.

> We should also add a version of CanListenToOpenTcpSocketHandle which sets OwnsHandle to false and verifies the server can successfully be started and stopped with the same handle twice. Otherwise, we have no test coverage for the new OwnsHandle API.

I'll add this test to the socket transport tests.

OK @halter73 I had to remove OwnsHandle because there's some weird behavior without it. The issue is that the accept loop doesn't properly yield when you dispose the listen socket. Not worth chasing down in this PR, I'll start a discussion with @stephentoub on dotnet runtime with an isolated repro.

issue_context.title: Implement UseSystemd with the SocketTransport
issue_context.body:
The BCL recently added support for creating a socket from a handle https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/34727. This enables us to implement Systemd socket activation without libuv.

cc @halter73 @shirhatti

review_comments: Would it be better to dispose the Socket first so it's not trying to utilize an already disposed handle?
